games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: According to “How to Make Bariis”, what happens if you lift the lid while the rice simmers?
choices: The rice browns and sticks to the base of the pot
The steam escapes and the rice stays hard
rounds.answer: The steam escapes and the rice stays hard
rounds.explanation: Step 7 states the consequence directly, because the trapped steam is what actually cooks the grains.

rounds.prompt: In “The Memory Wall”, why does Leo feel nervous at the start?
choices: He worries that he cannot remember anything exciting
He does not like his new classroom timetable
He has forgotten his pencil case at home
He would rather draw pictures than write about himself
rounds.answer: He worries that he cannot remember anything exciting
rounds.explanation: Leo asks that question aloud in part 1; wanting to draw instead is Nora's reaction, not his.

rounds.prompt: Nora stands at the fringe of the growing crowd. What does “fringe” mean there?
rounds.answer: The outer edge of it
rounds.explanation: Fringe names a border or outer edge, which is why Nora can watch the crowd without being inside it.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: In “What Makes Instructions Work”, which five parts does every strong set of instructions share?
choices: They share the title, the opening paragraph, the materials list, the numbered steps and the tips section.
It soaks in cold water for at least fifteen minutes, which softens the grains so they cook evenly.
He feels nervous, and the proof is his question, “What if I cannot remember anything exciting?”
rounds.answer: They share the title, the opening paragraph, the materials list, the numbered steps and the tips section.
rounds.explanation: The second paragraph names each part in turn and gives every one of them its own job.

rounds.prompt: Why does the bariis recipe warn you not to lift the lid while the rice is simmering?
choices: It soaks in cold water for at least fifteen minutes, which softens the grains so they cook evenly.
It means he paused before pinning his writing up, because he was unsure whether his memory was good enough.
Lifting the lid lets the steam escape, and the steam is what cooks the rice, so the grains stay hard.
rounds.answer: Lifting the lid lets the steam escape, and the steam is what cooks the rice, so the grains stay hard.
rounds.explanation: Step 7 states the cause and effect as a zero conditional, which is why the warning is a fact rather than a guess.

rounds.prompt: Nora tells Leo not to hesitate at the wall. What does “hesitate” mean at that moment in part 2?
choices: She means that working your way through a hard emotion takes real courage, so it deserves a place on the wall.
It means he paused before pinning his writing up, because he was unsure whether his memory was good enough.
The drained rice is added to the pot and stirred gently for two minutes until every grain is coated.
rounds.answer: It means he paused before pinning his writing up, because he was unsure whether his memory was good enough.
rounds.explanation: The narrator says a few pupils paused or hesitated, so the surrounding sentence supplies the meaning.

games.title: Question Quest
games.description: Read each unit question carefully and choose the best answer.

rounds.prompt: Where does the comma go in a conditional sentence?
choices: After the if-clause when it comes first
Before the word if in every sentence
After the main clause when the main clause comes first
Commas are never used in conditional sentences
rounds.answer: After the if-clause when it comes first
rounds.explanation: The comma marks the join only when the condition is stated first; reversing the halves removes the need for it.

rounds.prompt: Which of these is an imperative verb used in the bariis recipe?
rounds.answer: Drain
rounds.explanation: Drain is a base-form verb giving an order, while the others are an adverb, an adjective and a noun.

rounds.prompt: Which of these signals the order of the steps in a procedure?
rounds.answer: after that
rounds.explanation: After that is a time connective, whereas the others name an action, a colour and a piece of equipment.

games.title: Unit Mission
games.description: Finish with a mixed challenge across the whole unit.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence is a correct zero conditional?
choices: If you heat ice, it will melt.
If you heat ice, it melts.
If you heated ice, it melts.
If you will heat ice, it melts.
rounds.answer: If you heat ice, it melts.
rounds.explanation: The zero conditional puts the present simple in both halves, so no form of will and no past tense belongs there.

rounds.prompt: In a zero conditional, which tense do both halves of the sentence use?
rounds.answer: Present simple
rounds.explanation: The result is a permanent fact rather than a prediction, so both clauses stay in the present simple.

rounds.prompt: Which of these sentences is a first conditional rather than a zero conditional?
choices: If it rains, the ground gets wet.
If you heat metal, it expands.
If we leave now, we will be early.
If the temperature drops below zero, water freezes.
rounds.answer: If we leave now, we will be early.
rounds.explanation: Only this sentence predicts one particular future occasion, and the word will in the main clause is the giveaway.
